# Chapter Four: Rogan

> *"Man’s true enemy is not evil, the only true nemesis is fear itself."*
> — **Book of Aurtus**

The soldiers moved in perfect unison as the blonde haired chancellor looked upon the training grounds from the high window of the stone castle, the soldiers appeared as ants busying themselves over the grass, he could not help but nod at the surety of the analogy, for he was the second most powerful man in Western Dominance, these soldiers, mere pawns to his will.

Lord Veric Rogan smiled at the competence and surety of movement the soldiers exhibited as they worked through the morning ritual of training.

The sun had just moved beyond the horizon framing the buildings and the shadows of the large airships lumbered across the horizon, there holds laden with cargo and the promise of commerce.

His smile grew as he considered the money the crown would make from the cargo aboard those ships, the taxes alone would help fund the engine of war that was to come, soon he thought, the banner of the golden lioness would fly over the other dominances, bringing the kingdoms together as one.

The chancellor knew all, he ran the kingdom in the name his lady, his benefactor, his empress.

His steel blue eyes shone with the light some would recognize as fanaticism as he thought of the woman who had taken him under her wing and groomed him, making him the second most powerful person in all of Vicor.

Pulling the large fur coat tightly over his chest against the sudden gust of cold wind. He was careful not to disturb the black band that adorned his left bicep.

He stared at it blankly, worn for remembrance for the recent death of the emperor, though he did not mourn for the man, he had simply been an obstacle for his lady and one that Veric had gladly helped remove from her path, as he had done with so many he thought, the smile returning as he quietly named those who had been taken care of at the word of the only true ruler of Vicor, The Empress Victoria Augustus.

Veric Rogan was not an evil man, nor did he love killing, he understood that to serve the Empress and do her bidding was serving the whole of humanity.

So often he had sat with her, one of the many ancient texts that she had diligently collected draped across her lap as he listened with wonder her ruby lips flowed with the tales of the ancient world and their wondrous miracles. But also of the machine, the death machine that had been the undoing of mankind and the smile fell once again from his face.

He had listened to the stories of the fractured and warring countries that could not even come together under the common threat of extinction, instead opting to use the time to settle old scores and start new wars.

The Empress had so often explained the need to bring mankind under one rule, to bring about a lasting peace to allow them the ability to work towards the common defense, should the machine return. He had so often vowed to aid her and even now he was her soldier, her knight against those who would see her dream crumble.

Even the emperor himself had become such an obstacle, until Veric had ensured he wasn’t he reflected. Though the smile did not return, he did not enjoy the killing but only did it to ensure mankind’s continued existence, to bring about the peace the Empress had so often spoke of he thought.

“I am not interrupting, am I?” came a musical voice from the door dragging Veric from his thoughts.

Turning he quickly dropped to one knee and bowed his head deeply “No my Empress, simply lost in thought” he stated and waited as he listened to the sharp clap of well-tailored heels move across the marble floor. “Up my young lord, we have a lot of work to do” came the smiling voice as it finally ended its destination in front of the large stone fireplace and Rogan did as he was commanded, raising his head and getting to his feet to take in the vision that was his Empress. She was a vision of beauty standing erect with her long blonde hair, the Empress regarded the young man with a knowing smile.

“Empress, as you have requested all arrangements have been made for the emperor’s funeral, all invitations have been sent and his body will be displayed in the main hall beginning the day after next” Rogan began referring to the collection of notes held in his hand. The Empress waived a delicate hand dismissively “I just want to get it behind us Rogan, we have a lot to do, his passing was an unfortunate necessity” she said and he could hear the impatience in her voice, nodding he pushed on, not wanting to dwell on matters that would anger his Empress, that could be hazardous to his health.

“We have received letters of condolences as well as notifications of days of mourning for the emperor from Lusor and Dever” he stated and watched as her eyes narrowed. He knew her plans for the so-called neighbor states as he was sure their spies had reported the military buildup here in Vicor. “What do you wish me to respond?” he asked and braced himself for her wrath.

“Do nothing, nothing at all” she merely answered but he could hear the edge in her tone, knew the letters bothered her but again let it go, best not dwell on that which would draw the wrath of a woman who could have him killed with a simple waive of her hand.

He had no illusion about it, he knew he was her favorite but also knew that she was subject to her own impulses and sometimes though she would feel regret later, would make a rash decision in the moment.

Aurtus knows he had been the one to clean up such actions or to make them right. “How are the emperor’s advisors fairing? “She asked a hint of a smile forming on the edge of her mouth. Rogan shook his head in mock sorry.

“Apparently a few of them had died due to accidents and one was robbed in our very own capital and killed, leaving only two who remain” he stated and watched as the Empress’s smile grew “Well, we will have to look into that” she simple stated and turned towards the fire, Rogan taking a moment to appreciate her silhouette.

It had been a very busy week, once the emperor had been taken care of, his advisors had met, planning and scheming to remove the Empress, to take power for themselves and Rogan was forced to act, gutting the power base and removing those who would try to go against his Empress, now with only two remaining, there power neutered they were no longer a threat he reflected, watching the Empress.

“I am to talk to Ambassador Gurin this afternoon my Empress, he is meeting with members of the Turen government” at this her head snapped up and Rogan made a calming motion with his hand. “Fear not, I have the matter well in hand” he stated, one of her dead husbands’ advisors meeting with the government of a rival kingdom did not sit well with her and he knew it, but he also knew that the man would not live through the day regardless of what he told them.

With a sigh he pulled the last sheet he had in his hand and brace himself “This brings me to the outcasts my Empress, they, once again are asking to meet with you about the conditions in the village” he stated and watched as she tensed up. She had never liked the miners, one of her husband’s pet projects, the Outcasts were the lifeblood of the crystal industry and they both knew it, without them the flow of crystals for ships, weapons and everything else that required power would stop.

The Outcasts had been a point of contention for generations, forced by the emperors grandfather to work the mine due to the exposure those who spent their lives mining the crystals that ran the empire changed, they had been altered and could no longer truly call themselves human. Because of this they had been relegated to a town outside of the mine, never allowed to leave the crown fed them and sheltered them. They not only grew the crystals, but by crushing them to dust they would grow the necessary gravity spires and other crystals, mixing dust and other items to grow the hybrids, recipes that very few knew but were required to make the machines that powered mankind.

Over the years the support waned for the miners, and they had now begun to complain, Rogan felt pity for them, but the Empress hated them with a passion. “Up their food and no more, I don’t want to hear from them Rogan, not now” she simply said, and he bowed, making a note on the sheet of paper.

“Now, if you have nothing else my Empress, I must take my leave to ensure that I handle certain people in a timely fashion” Rogan stated bowing as the Empress waived a hand dismissively. With a deep bow he left his Empress standing by the fire. Exiting the room, he turned left walking by his own office door and heading for the main foyer. The expansive stone halls stretched into the distance as he made his way past servants and knights scuttling along the hall as the life of the castle continued ever forward.

The foyer was a large stone room, meant to intimidate all who entered, four guards stood post at each corner of the room facing the center where a giant silver beast stood facing the large opening.

Rogan was never sure what or who had made it, but it had stood there for the decades he had lived at the castle, never changing and never moving. It stood two stories almost reaching the ceiling of the foyer, it was a human form and would have been dismissed as a statue of one ruler or god save the head, it was twice the size of any normal one and the horns that circled the side of the face were most definitely not human.

Rogan followed the line of the metal sculpture to its terminating point near the ceiling, admiring once again its massive size as he walked out into the cold morning air of the capital.

Moving down the steps into the expansive center of the Capital Rogan stopped to admire the life of the large city, it had an energy to it, once that he admired and worshipped, watching he saw carts and buggies whirring by as they moved packages and goods from one end of the city to the next, the platoons of soldiers walked along the main road in formation going from one such training or another, there gold and silver armor glistening in the morning sun.

Overhead Airships continued to move in and out of the capital, he often thought of this place as the heart of the kingdom, pumping the life blood of information and commerce to the rest of the body. “Lord Chancellor Rogan” came a baritone voice from in front of him and snapping out of his thoughts he looked to regard the tall gaunt man standing in a black suit.

Behind him was a large silver box with wheels, a buggy, one of the contraptions that had emerged over the last decade, not stout enough to make the journey across the kingdom but one that was used often to move about the capital, one of the many uses for the Crystals the outcast mined he mused, moving towards the man and the buggy.

The man stepped to the side and opened the door allowing Rogan entry, he knew Loric, his assistant had his schedule, so the appearance of the driver and buggy did not surprise him in the least. The tall dark driver walked confidently around the buggy and climbed into the drivers set. He flipped a switch and turned two dials, as Rogan watched the dashboard began to pulse green as the crystals moved together and unleashing the energy that turned the crank.

After a moment the driver pulled a lever, engaging the driveshaft and the buggy lurched forward. “Where to my Lord?” the driver asked. “Foreign district, let me off near the park” Rogan said, raising his voice over the wind of the open cab. The wind drowned out the barely audible whirring of the crystals as the buggy sped up, weaving in and out of others like it and the horse and carriages that were still the staple of travel in the capital.

Rogan pulled his coat tight against the cold air as it passed through the open cab and watched the people and vehicles as they went about their business. After twenty minutes of driving the buggy pulled over and the driver walked around the gleaming metal cab, opening the door for the Chancellor.

Stepping out of the buggy Rogan took in the grand park in the foreign district, the home of the Embassies for Turen and Lusor as well as others, as he looked upon the large square that made up the block he could see the squat four story stone buildings with their tall walls, the sovereign territory of the other powers right here in the center of the capital he mused. Here he would find the traitor Gurin, fresh from his meeting he thought, moving into the park as the buggies whir picked tempo as it moved into traffic disappearing amongst the myriad of other crystal and horse powered conveyances.

He entered the park, making his way among the few visitors on this cold morning, the trees were all stripped of leaves as were most of the plants, giving the normally beautiful park a barren look as he proceeded up the cobblestones further into park towards the large pond that adorned the center.

He stepped to the stone ledge that surrounded the large pond, looking over the water he stood there lost in his thoughts for the moment “Chancellor” came a familiar voice behind him and Rogan grimaced “Lord Gurin, how are you this fine day” he finally said, trying to make the statement sound casual though he felt anything but. The older man stepped up next to Rogan, his larger frame casting a shadow and removing what little warmth the sun offered.

Rogan turn to look at the man, his white hair shoulder length framed a normally pleasant face, the laugh lines deep from much use, but he was anything but pleasant or jovial that morning. “I take it the Empress sent you to dispatch me after my meeting” he said, no emotion, just a statement but Rogan still winced.

He had known Lord Gurin for many years and had considered him a friend, but the man had crossed the line, meeting with the enemy after all was tant amount to treason. “You went too far my Lord, how did you think this would end?” he whispered, just loud enough for the other man to hear him. Gurin stood there silently for a moment, both men looking out over the water.

“Do you know what she is planning, have you seen the tower?” the old Lord whispered to him “Do you understand what her plans are and what they will do to this land Rogan?” he finished and the other man stood silent. What tower he thought, but he had understood what he needed to know, what she had told him and what he had done to ensure that her will was made manifest.

“We need to come together Gurin, we need a single leader, our land is fractured and while we squabble, dangers threaten us, she only wants to ensure our survival” Rogan answered and could hear the old man chuckle. “That’s not what this is about, you don’t know what she had done do you?” he asked turning to face Rogan.

“Then there is still hope for your soul” Gurin began, but before he could finish, before he could utter another word, Rogan stepped in and slid the dagger he had palmed into the man’s belly. Gurin gasped his eyes wide as he looked down at the blood that began to cover the white shirt he wore. “You betrayed her Gurin, for that you will die, anything else you have to say, you can say to Aurtus himself” Rogan whispered before sliding the dagger out and moving away as Gurin fell to his knees behind him.

Rogan walked out of the park, turning left he pulled the coat tight against the cold and began to make his way back towards the silhouette of the palace in the distance.

An hour later Rogan had made it back to the castle, upon returning he went straight to his office, entering the outer chamber he found it full of newly acquired ledgers stacked over every surface of the place. “Loric, where are you boy?” the Lord Chancellor called annoyed with his assistant, the boy seemed to spawn ledgers, every day more seemed to show up he thought. A stack of ledgers hit the floor as the young overweight noble came out from behind the desk, quickly falling to his knees picking up the ledgers that littered the floor.

“I’m sorry Lord, I will have these cleaned up in a moment, I was just going through the financial ledgers from last week, I hope to have them done soon, I promise” the young man stammered.

Rogan shook his head “How is it whenever I leave and return it seems you have accumulated more of these damned Ledgers” he stated shaking his head.

“Well, my Lord everything that happens or is purchased in the castle must pass through this office for approval, it’s a lot of stuff” he finished flashing a sheepish smile at his boss the expression on the earnest chubby face almost endearing he thought.

Rogan made a mock disgusted noise and walked into his own chambers, closing the door on the young man and his mess. With a sigh he walked over to the large wooden desk and sat down behind it, rubbing his temples as he tried to banish the coming headache.

Looking down at the desk, he spotted the lone quill sitting there, focusing his mind he concentrated on the small object watching at first as it vibrated then coming to stand on end slowly as he pushed at the small quill, finally it fell Rogan falling back with exhaustion, he had never told anyone about his ability, not that it was very impressive unless he was playing dice he supposed, at the ripe age of thirteen he first discovered his ability to move small objects, well moving them was a grand word for what he did more like shift them quite by accident.

He had never told his father or his brother, both already disapproving of him Rogan had heard stories of the mages the ones who ran the crystal smithy’s and worked as healers, everyone one of them branded and outcast by society but there gifts and wares needed so they were tolerated. His father would never suffer his son being a spell caster, he had decided it was best if he did not mention it, Shaking off the weariness he looked over the docket of his day realizing he would not be done until late into the night, such was the job of the Chancellor he thought and then puffed up a bit with pride, not just Chancellor, but Grand Chancellor, youngest ever appointed he thought smiling.

He ran the castle, hell he ran the kingdom anything that required the Empress’s attention had to get through him first which meant he was the one whom the Lords would try and curry favor with, plying him with gifts and information making him the centerpiece of the entire court. There was nothing that happened that Rogan did not know. Rogan sat there reflecting on the Empress and her intentions.

Soon the Empress would move against her neighbors and the kingdom would once again expand Rogan would be the key figure of power, reporting to only the Empress he thought smiling it began to falter as he thought about his father again how he would disapprove of the empress’s plans citing honor and nobility but he wouldn’t let that thought ruin the good mood that he had found himself in, which was not something that happened often when meeting with the Black Empress he mused. “My Lord” Loric whispered peaking his head in the door and almost leaving again when he saw the annoyed look on his master’s face

“What is it Loric?” Rogan asked exasperated as he continued to rub at his temples. “My Lord, Master Jurin has requested to see you, he is here now, should I tell him to come back later?” Loric asked and Rogan stopped rubbing as he looked surprised at the young man.

What could the Empress’s spymaster want with him he wondered “Show him in Loric” Rogan said, and the young man disappeared. A moment later a short pudgy man with a pleasant face entered the office his bright robes and pleasant face was at odds with the man’s position as the Empress’s spy master he thought as the other man sang a hello and came to perch in the chair across from Rogan, not sitting he noticed, but perched as if he were a colorful bird the smile never leaving his face. But Rogan wasn’t fooled, he knew the type of jobs this man did and he, more than once had to clean up after one of this man’s more exuberant questioning sessions and the aftermath of that was still seared in his mind he thought with a quiet shiver.

“Master Jurin, to what do I owe this pleasant surprise” Rogan said keeping his face guarded but pleasant as he sat back and regarded the other man. The two sat there regarding each other for nearly five minutes before the little unassuming spymaster finally spoke, his soft delicate voice a contrast to his large frame.

Leaning in conspiratorially he spoke “A little bird told me the Empress has troops looking into something that fell from the sky, and from what I hear they aren’t the only ones” he began, and Rogan leaned back. Playing games with this man was dangerous he recalled regarding the unassuming man who, with one word could have him killed, despite his position and power.

“What have you heard?” Rogan asked casually carefully watching his face as the man formed a response. Jurin revealed nothing as he stared at Rogan the small smile never leaving his face “My lord I hear many, many things not all of them credible, but when I hear those things that I feel the Empress might be interested in, I bring them to you as I serve at her pleasure, I have heard that our neighbors have dispatched troops to find this thing, also the Mages at Dragon’s keep have sent out a few of their own trackers, now whatever did make its way down from the heavens seems to interest everyone very much” he finished slightly bowing his head in deference to Rogan’s power.

“What do you know about the thing the Empress searches for and why everyone is so determined to find it?” Jurin asked, his tone was casual, but Rogan had known the man long enough to know that any question he asked was far from small talk and narrowed his eyes at the man.

“Not much at all Lord Jurin, just that she instructed me to find out what had come down, however when things like this happen, we find rocks in those locations, nothing more, as if the gods are playing a joke on us with some game we don’t know the rules of” he stated. Jurin knew of the other man’s instructions and if he didn’t know about them then he wasn’t worth the gold paid to him Rogan thought. Jurin smiled that annoying knowing smile of his the one that said he pitied any mere mortal who didn’t have all the information they needed.

Rogan had to force himself not to roll his eyes. “What do you know Jurin, I tire of these games” Rogan stated allowing the annoyance to drip into his words the other man’s smile widening as if in this game, he was winning.

“Lord Rogan, I am surprised the Empress had not apprised you of the severity of this search or that there were others whom search for that which had landed. I will tell you that what has landed is worth more than gold my friend expeditions have been sent from not only Vicor, Lusor, Dever and Dragons Keep but also a few enterprising lords have dispatched their own groups, I think whoever discovers it, will have a decided edge on the coming events. In fact, our own Lord Advisor Guren might have been the source of the information to the other countries, I am sure you are familiar with his accident early this morning” Jurin said eyeing the other man with barely veiled suspicion.

Rogan thought of the conversation, the gravity that the Empress had implied this search contained, this was not something he could leave to other nations to find he realized, and what could the Mages want with it he mused, but he had to be careful when dealing with the likes of Jurin he thought.

Rogan did not let anything show on his face but cursed internally, how did this man know about the teams from Lusor and Dever, also did he have spies in the Mages keep he wondered if so, that would be quite a feat.

The Empress had not trusted him with the information he thought anger flashing into his thoughts but quickly suppressed, it would not do to show this man his true feelings. On the outside Rogan simply leaned back regarding the books behind Jurin.

“How do you know this?” he simply asked the uncomfortable feeling of being left out settling in on his mind. Rogan shifted uncomfortably in his seat Jurin catching the action and again renewing his smile. Can he know what I am thinking Rogan wondered still eyeing the little man. Jurin leaned a little forward his eyes roving around almost conspiratorially

“I am going to do you a favor Lord Rogan, I am going to let you in on the political games that are currently in play that you remain ignorant to and a search for a weapon that could turn the tide in the coming war that our Empress wishes to instigate, however I am unsure if she is aware of these… things” he said and again Rogan narrowed his eyes “what’s your cost Spymaster, you give nothing for free” he stated evenly.

Jurin smiled “Oh, my payment is you knowing and reporting back to me anything you hear on this subject, do we have a deal Lord Rogan”. The young Lord thought about this for a moment, when you made an agreement with this man you honored it for the consequences for not, well they would make his early morning activities look like a picnic.

Finally, he nodded once “I agree, now tell me what is going on” he said matching the other man by leaning forward. “You have heard the stories, those with the gift that would have them taken by the mages guild have gone missing, the mages are at a loss to understand who is taking there initiates” He asked the other man and Rogan laughed, trying to keep the nervousness out of his tone, did this man know about him he wondered but outwardly he scoffed. “I have heard the rumors, merely conspiracy theories” he scoffed but his smile quickly died as he noticed Jurin was not laughing, in fact he looked serious.

“You can’t be serious?” He asked and Jurin nodded did this man know about Rogan’s own powers he thought doing his best to keep panic off his face. “Those with the gift get rarer every year and despite the agreement with the crown that the Mages of the keep train then, mark them and allow them back into the world, there are those that feel one could gain a decided advantage should he unlock the secret of the powers of the Magi and more so train their own who have loyalty to them and not the Keep” he continued, and Rogan leaned back thinking, taking people like him he wondered. If the Empress did not know about this, then he had a responsibility to find out as much as he could, besides if there were others like him didn’t, he has a duty to find out what was happening to them he thought.

“Preposterous, if there was a secret project, authorized by the crown, I would know about it” he said irritated at the insinuation that the Empress was keeping things from him. Jurin cocked his head “So you know all of the details of Galen’s mission and what it is he is looking for?” the other man asked and then leaned back “Besides, who said the Empress even knows about it” and Rogan’s face fell She was keeping that close to the vest, but the other statement hit more to home, what if some of the Lords aligned against her were doing this, he had to know he thought vowing to look into it.

The look on his face was answer enough for Jurin.

“Do you recall the story about the ancients who sent the first men to earth in their tears?” he asked, and Rogan nodded. “Everyone knew that story, it was a basic tenant of WIC how the second coming of man came to be, Metal tears fell from the sky carrying the first humans of the second age of man” he summed up for the other man. Jurin looked at him for a moment regarding him as if deciding something, after a moment he nodded to himself and continued “This is not just a story, I have reports going back fifty years, twice things seen in the sky were metal containers, in which people emerged, people who were rumored to have extraordinary power, then they just disappear, without a trace. I have yet to ascertain where they go or with whom. But I have every confidence this is what the Empress suspects landed and she is moving mountains to ensure she contains and captures whatever came out of that container” he finished Rogan kept his face neutral the Empress had told him how potentially important it was she find out and get what had come down, he could not allow someone else get ahold of it if it was that critical to her plans he mused

“Are you saying that these people are sent by the gods?” he asked carefully and Jurin rolled his eyes “No, but they come from somewhere, I am sure there is a logical explanation, but one we are unaware of. Whatever the case, nations are clamoring to find these people, as to what they do with them I don’t know. But that is where you come in my Dear Rogan, with what I have given you, you can find out what is going on and when you do, you will report it back to me” he stated his face going serious and Rogan could see the implied warning in those eyes.

Jurin stood quickly “good day Lord Rogan, but remember, whatever you find might change your life forever, ensure that when you look into this, it’s what you want to do, trust no one” he stated, the ominous statement of his words clear as he turned and then walked out of the office, leaving the stunned Rogan sitting behind his desk staring after him.

He spent almost an hour pondering what the other man had said then recalled the last words Gurin had spoken, where they connected, did these me know something he as the Chancellor did not he wondered, was it possible that one of the Lords could have a project of such scale and keep it well under the radar of not only the Empress, but also himself, more so didn’t he have an obligation and a duty to do whatever it took to uncover that project, despite the possibility he might inadvertently come across information the Empress felt he wasn’t ready for he considered this for a while and his answer was simple, of course he was.

What if the thing they were looking for was a person and that person held the power of the first men, what would that mean for whoever captured them? There had been reports of squads of troops seen in the vicinity of Hovath a village to the west of the location he had sent men. Hovath was just a stone throw from the border with Dever he thought. Could they be sending people to retrieve this person or thing he pondered. But how would he find out, then it hit him, the reason Jurin had come to him. Any expenditure in the kingdom came across his desk, would someone hide this in plain sight he wondered, if they had then he had all the information he needed, now he just had to find it. Sticking his head out of the door he found his young assistant hard at work reviewing ledgers, his face smeared with ink, as he absently touched his face while taking notes, the look was almost comical Rogan thought.

“I want every ledger for every expenditure for the last two years in my office” he stated and then slammed the door, leaving the wide-eyed young man gaping at him. He knew he had taken little interest in the books and thus the reason he had hired his young assistant so he wouldn’t have to, but now, somewhere in there was the beginning of an answer he needed he thought.

The sun had set hours ago as Rogan sat at his desk the Crystal lamp lighting the page he was reviewing. He jotted another note into the small notebook that had pages of small sentences, names and locations. Rubbing his eyes now burning from lack of sleep he sat back, looking at the small notebook. He had found more than a few charges and expenditures that didn’t make sense unless you accounted for at least one project someone wanted kept off the books, the name wasn’t familiar to him and he knew every high Lord in the court, which meant only one thing, someone was using a proxy he thought. Rogan had gone back almost two decades in his search This project had been going on a long time he thought, since almost after the death of the emperor he realized. He sighed as he looked over the notes. Jurin had set him on a very dangerous path, he was searching for information on a project he was not authorized to see, if he were caught there was no talking his way out of it. The first thing he needed to do, was connect this signature with someone real, but the likelihood of that was next to impossible, but the money had to go to something he thought. The Entries in the notebook was something he could follow.

There was enough information to where he should be able to find either a location or something that was purchased with the gold given by the crown, but that meant finding someone who was more an expert at this then he Rogan thought.

At that moment a low knock came at his door and Rogan looked around curiously, who could know he was here this late. Then a slight wave of fear came over him what if Jurin had decided that he was too much of a risk.

Rogan put his hand in the drawer grabbing the ivory handled pistol in the drawer his paranoia at an all-time high at the moment “Come in” he said aiming the gun at the general direction of the door. It opened slowly and a young male assistant popped his head in “My Lord, I have a missive from the recon captain you sent out earlier, it was marked urgent so I brought it over meaning to leave it on the desk of your assistant, but then saw the light, I hope I am not disturbing you” the young assistant said and Rogan could see the trepidation and fear in his voice. With an annoyed expression he waved the young man over, the fear draining from him. But he kept his hand on the gun until the assistant left the message and walked out of the office.

Rogan picked it up and read it over. He read it over and then read it again. They were traveling but have seen more than one group of black troops traveling the area and needed clarification if those were ours, Black troops he thought remembering the term, when a house or lord wished to complete a task and not have it linked to them, they would remove all sigils from the soldier’s uniform, giving them in essence a black, blank tunic.

He scrawled a note notifying them if any troops were seen they were to be captured and interrogated and then marked the message as urgent, it would get to the Empress in the morning when she woke, if she approved it would be forwarded to the troops.

Rogan left the office, going to his quarters as he carefully poured over his notes. Going to the earliest notes he found the purchase of a property, this one didn’t have a location or name, he knew all the properties that the monarchy owned having reviewed the assets of the crown during his first months on the job, back when he thought that paperwork was going to be his life. But this one wasn’t listed except the note “The Tower” attached to it.

Soon after that he began to see small sets of mercenaries who were paid, at the same time pouring over reports from villages he could match missing people and then soldiers dispatched to remove families for “treasonous activity” some were killed, some were exiled. Rogan could not see a pattern as to which one’s were let off easier than the others. But in all cases at least one member of the family was removed, basically disappeared he noted. If he was going to find out what this was about, he had to find the tower, and he knew someone who would know where and what it was he thought closing the notebook.

The night was cold as he left the castle, bundling up the large coat as he made his way into the village that surrounded the large stone keep. Guards looked at him and quickly avoided eye contact once they realized who he was. No one would bother him this night, they knew he held the confidence of the Empress and if he were out late, then they didn’t want to know what he was up to Rogan thought with an ironic smile as he walked down alley after alley looking for an address he had not visited in years.

Hopefully he was still alive Rogan worried. After half an hour of navigating the small narrow alleys of dark homes lined up next to each other, he found the one he was looking for. Rogan walked up to the door and pounded loudly, after a few moments he did it again. It wasn’t until the third knock that he heard the distant shuffling of motion in the small dilapidated home. The door opened revealing an old gentleman with tousled hair and bleary eyes

“What is it” he snapped before he noticed Rogan standing on the stoop. His demeanor quickly changed, the old man smiling at his student and once friend “Juric?, I’m sorry Lord Rogan” he corrected Rogan smiled “Horst, you can always call me Juric, may I come in” he asked and the man who had held his job previously, the one who had taught him everything he ever needed to know about administering a government moved slowly out of the way to allow Rogan entry.

Walking into the small house the heady smell of spices used for curing ailments in the old permeated his nostrils as he surveyed the stacks of papers and books that seemed to have taken over the entire living area.

Kilren Horst had once been the most important man in the kingdom, the right hand of the emperor himself, when the Empress had taken over, she had appointed a very young and inexperienced Juric Rogan to the job. Kilren had taken the young scared Lord under his wing and taught him everything he needed to know to navigate the treacherous waters of politics and finance in the court before retiring. Rogan winced as he looked around the impoverished house that the old man now resided in.

“My friend, I have some questions and they are ones only you can answer, may we sit” Rogan asked, and Kilren Horst nodded, motioning Rogan towards the living room, he cleared off two chairs of papers and took one, Rogan taking the other. “What can I do for you Juric, I assume you are not here on official business as the hour isn’t one most people do proper work” he stated arching his eyebrow but still smiling at his friend.

Rogan nodded returning the smile and with a sigh began “There is a property, that was purchased, it is not listed on any official document except for the purchase, the only note, I recognize the handwriting, it was your note my friend simply said ‘The Tower’” he finished and instantly he could see the change in the old man.

He sat silently avoiding eye contact with Rogan as if he were thinking “You don’t want to go down this path Juric, this is not something you want to know, because once you find out, you cannot unknow it” Kilren said cryptically. Rogan leaned in “So you know the property?” he asked getting excited and Kilren nodded “Don’t ask me the question Juric, I will answer it if you do, but trust me in this, you don’t want to know anymore then you already do, if you have been told of this, pointed at it then things will change for you, you might not be ready. I tell you this as a friend” he finished, and Rogan paused the man’s tone was serious and almost what pained he thought as he looked at his friend curiously.

“I have to know Kilren, please tell me” Rogan whispered. Lord Horst nodded but keeping his head lowered.

“I was instructed to find a property, I will not reveal by who, I have given my word, one that was not to be on the official rosters, I was to purchase it and then hide all knowledge of it” Kilren began his voice monotone, totally devoid of emotion as if he were giving a deposition and Rogan leaned closer.

“Go on” he whispered listening to the old man. “I found the place in Giren, near the shore. It was an old keep made for a long dead lord. I purchased it, repaired it, upgraded it to the requested specifications, installing cells and equipment for some kind of research. I then recruited the best Crystal Smiths and doctors in the Kingdom; I hid all of this and was then told to forget about it. But I couldn’t my curiosity got the better of me a year later and I went to the property what I saw Juric, I can’t even speak of it, however if you go there, you will never be the same again” the old man said cryptically.

“I was let go soon after and told if I talked about it, I would be killed, I don’t care anymore Juric. I am too old to care; I will give you the location and do with it what you want” he said tears coming to the old man’s eyes. He had never seen Kelrin cry not in all the years he had known the man Rogan thought, this more than anything bothering him, There were only a few people who had the power to do what he explained had been requested of him, Rogan did not dwell on this, nor did he asks his friend for fear he would not like the answer, instead he focused on the property.

He left the house an hour later, a piece of parchment in his pocket with the directions to the secret tower burning a hole in his pocket. He had to know what had happened to those like him, what could break a man like Kelrin he thought. Rogan returned to his quarters resolving to make a plan to go to this tower and discover what the secret was.
